drafts.title: Front seats provide extended thigh support and reliable memory recall for tall drivers
drafts.description: When a tall driver enters the car they feel full thigh support from the front seat cushion and their saved seat position is restored reliably every time without manual fine-adjustment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion offers an adjustable thigh-support extension of at least 60 mm compared with the current model baseline, and the driver seat memory restores the saved position within ±10 mm fore/aft and ±5° backrest for 99% of attempts across 100 consecutive save/restore cycles, including after ignition off/on.
assumptions: 60 mm extension provides meaningful additional thigh support for drivers up to ~195 cm tall (assumes current baseline measured on current 5 Series).
Seat position sensors and actuators can achieve the stated positional tolerances with existing architecture.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort depends on foam/fabric and personal preference beyond geometric support.
Long-term sensor/calibration drift may affect restore tolerance and needs durability validation.

drafts.title: Rear seating delivers legroom at least as generous as main competitors
drafts.description: Rear-seat occupants experience class-competitive legroom so rear passengers (including tall adults) do not feel cramped compared with main rivals.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear legroom (knee point to seat back) is at least 970 mm, measured per ISO seating reference, with production vehicles meeting this value within ±5 mm.
assumptions: 970 mm is representative of main competitors' published rear legroom and is a realistic target for packaging in the successor 5 Series.
uncertainties: Final achievable value depends on platform packaging and optional wheelbase/seat position configurations.

drafts.title: Interior convenience: cup holders fit large bottles and trunk has a usable 12 V outlet for coolers
drafts.description: Customers can store common large bottles securely in the center console cup holders and can power a portable cooler from a trunk socket without needing adapters or workarounds.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Center console cup holders securely accommodate containers up to 95 mm diameter and keep a 1 L bottle upright under 0.3 g longitudinal deceleration; trunk includes an accessible 12 V socket capable of supplying at least 8 A continuous and demonstrated to run a 12 V cooler drawing 8 A for 2 hours while the trunk is closed.
assumptions: 95 mm diameter covers common large tumblers and 1 L bottles used by customers.
8 A continuous is sufficient for typical small portable 12 V coolers customers expect to run from the trunk.
uncertainties: Some high-power coolers may draw >8 A; customers with those devices will need higher-capacity power or an inverter.
Cup-holder effectiveness depends on occupant ergonomics and optional center console variants.

drafts.title: Hands‑free tailgate opens reliably on the first attempt
drafts.description: When a customer performs the hands-free foot gesture the tailgate opens promptly and reliably without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under standard conditions (ambient 0–35 °C, dry ground), a valid hands-free foot gesture opens the tailgate within 2 seconds on the first attempt in at least 95% of 100 consecutive gesture tests.
assumptions: Standard conditions exclude heavy snow/ice or obstructed sensors; gesture performed at typical distance and height.
Gesture definition and detection zone are consistent with current customer usage patterns.
uncertainties: Performance may degrade in heavy rain, snow, or with unusual footwear; these conditions should be validated separately.

drafts.title: Rich, adjustable ambient lighting with many colors and brightness levels
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior mood lighting with a wide palette and fine-grained brightness control per zone (driver, front passenger, rear).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting offers at least 64 selectable colors and 10 distinct brightness steps per zone, with per-zone selection (driver/front passenger/rear) and color/brightness changes applied within 1 second of selection.
assumptions: LED modules and vehicle electrical architecture available for the successor can support 64 colors and 10 brightness steps per zone.
User interface will expose per-zone controls in the lighting settings.
uncertainties: Perceived color fidelity varies by trim materials and ambient light; final implementation may require calibration per trim.
Some legacy trim packages may limit available zones.

drafts.title: Door handles and flush-release systems operate reliably in freezing weather
drafts.description: Customers can open the doors in cold, freezing-weather conditions without handles sticking or needing manual thawing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: After exposure to freezing precipitation and temperatures down to -20 °C, flush and conventional door handles open on the first attempt in at least 98% of tests without requiring manual thawing or secondary force.
assumptions: Test exposure simulates realistic freezing precipitation (ice accretion) and standard customer use.
-20 °C is a representative severe-cold target for primary markets (US cold regions).
uncertainties: Extreme ice accumulation beyond test severity or user-applied de-icing chemicals may still impede operation.
Design choices (flush vs. fixed handles) affect achievable robustness and may require trade-offs with aerodynamics.
